content: Multi-stage pipeline diagnostic reports follow a consistent structure across ML and FDA analysis contexts: (1) per-stage diagnostics block — method name, key scalars, quality flags; (2) inter-stage transition summary — how the output of one stage feeds the next (e.g. smoothed representation quality affects FPCA variance explained); (3) aggregated summary — overall pipeline health flag, list of flagged issues across stages, single narrative paragraph; (4) sources/traceability — each cited value traced to its fdars-computed origin. Good report structure: ordered by analysis pipeline stages (represent → smooth → cluster/regress → monitor); each stage has its own diagnostics block; cross-stage signals (e.g. poor smoothing causing inflated FPCA components) are surfaced in the transition layer; the overall narrative synthesises stage signals without repeating per-stage detail. FDA-specific pipeline stages map to existing advisor aspects: represent (aspect #represent), smooth (aspect #smoothing), FPCA (aspect #fpca), clustering (aspect #clustering), regression (aspect #regression), inference/monitoring (aspects #inference, #spm). A pipeline report is therefore an aggregation of N build_diagnostics calls (one per stage) plus an LLM call that takes the full diagnostics dict-of-dicts and produces a multi-aspect Advice. The key new data structure: a list of (stage_name, diagnostics_dict) pairs, one per completed stage.
